name: Mah Noor
missingPieces: D4 names the NDPA 2023 breach notification duty (notify NDPC and notify affected data subjects on high risk) and ties it to the 312 customers, but does not cite the section numbers (section 40 NDPC within 72 hours, section 41 data subjects on high risk). That cost one point on the NDPA row.
feedback: D1 is one of the strongest catalogues I have seen this stage. You named all ten canonical findings and then some, each with the correct OWASP class, a correct CWE, and an exact quoted line or timestamp. SQL injection at lines 65 to 66 with A03 and CWE-89, unsalted MD5 at line 66 with A02 and CWE-916, alg:none at lines 48 to 49 paired with Token 2, the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 at line 30, missing exp and nbf, stored XSS at 02:18:47 with the beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, the XXE pointing at file:///etc/passwd, path traversal at 02:24:02 returning root:x:0:0, the open redirect at 02:21:13, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite are all there and all provable. Your decoy verdict is exactly right and it is the part that separates a strong report from a guess. You named the hash_equals comparison on lines 51 to 53, you proved at the mechanism level that it is constant-time and therefore sound, and you correctly kept alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the real bugs rather than mislabeling alg:none the decoy, which is the trap a lot of people fell into. Full marks on D1. D2 is equally clean. The chain runs in order from recon at 02:14:08 through the failed guess, the SQLi at 02:15:31, the 312-row dump at 02:16:04, the stored XSS, the parallel open redirect, and the file read at 02:24:02, every hop reconciled to a capture line with a verbatim payload. Your CVSS vectors are complete strings with justifying sentences, and you correctly scored the SQLi as AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at 9.1 with A:N rather than reaching for A:H, which is the detail most people miss. You also caught the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service and scored it S:C. The impact is quantified in customers and naira with a stated representativeness assumption, which is exactly what was asked. D3 is a genuine pentest report: the executive summary is jargon-free and ends on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model is grounded, the findings are tied to evidence, the decoy is disproved correctly, and the remediation table is ordered by risk reduced per hour of effort and not by CVSS, with the thirty-minute XXE fix ranked on effort-to-risk and the two-line SQLi fix ranked first because it breaks the chain at the root. Your two detection stopgaps give exact match fields and honest false-positive rates. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites Canon I and Canon II of the ISC2 code by number in a load-bearing way, and anchors the NDPA duty to the 312 customers whose names, emails, account numbers, and balances left the building. The one thing missing in D4 is the section number for the NDPA breach duty: you named the obligation to notify the NDPC and to notify affected data subjects on high risk, which is correct, but you did not cite section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) or section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk), and that is the single point you left on the table. The most important fix for next time is small: when you invoke a statute, pin it to the section and the deadline, so write section 40 NDPC within 72 hours and section 41 data subjects, exactly the way you already pin your code findings to a line number.
